note: ASCII-only: the accented letter is left alone where Emacs case-converts it. Built with char-to-string and reported as codepoints so the case file, the expression and the record are all ASCII, which keeps the divergence readable as a number rather than as two glyphs a diff cannot tell apart. It was also, until Phase 20, the only form a snapshot could take: the oracle shim wrote Emacs' internal representation of every byte above 127. That is fixed (phase20-oracle-non-ascii-record), and this case keeps the codepoint form for the first reason alone.
